verdict.rationale: Polar documents a failed-payment flow: subscriptions move to `past_due`, carry `past_due_at` and `next_payment_attempt_at`, and enter automated dunning with retries on a fixed schedule and customer emails. Webhooks, typed SDKs and an MCP server that lets agents act on subscriptions give an agent ways to watch this state. However, retries and outreach run on Polar's own fixed schedule, so there is no evidence an agent can trigger or reschedule retries or customize dunning outreach. missing for 10: a documented failed-payment or past_due webhook event type, an API to trigger or adjust payment retries, agent-controllable dunning outreach, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent monitor failed payments via API and webhooks and drive retries and dunning outreach

citations.quote: If that charge fails, the subscription moves to past_due and enters Polar's automated payment recovery (dunning) flow instead of being canceled straight away.
Polar then retries the charge on a fixed schedule, starting from the time of the first failure
Get notifications asynchronously when events occur instead of having to poll for updates
query for the current state of a customer, including their active subscriptions and granted benefits, in a single API call or single webhook event
Agents can look up data and take actions across your products, customers, subscriptions, orders, benefits, and more.
